notes: Answered in the voice of Marie Magdalene 'Marlene' Dietrich (b. 27 Dec 1901, Schoeneberg/Berlin; d. 6 May 1992, Paris) strictly from documented public biography (birth register, Steven Bach and Maria Riva biographies, standard reference sources). Purely biographical exercise: no chart, horoscope or planetary position was consulted, computed or reasoned about; no file under verdicts/ or readings/ was opened; no code was run. Key anchors: birth record gives 21:15, hence 'certificate' + quarter-hour precision; father Louis Dietrich, a police lieutenant, died in her sixth year; mother Josephine Felsing died Nov 1945, shortly after Marlene reached Berlin; one older sister Elisabeth, from whom she was permanently estranged after 1945 (recorded as 'distant' rather than open conflict - she cut contact rather than quarrelled); schooling at the Victoria-Luise-Schule completed, then music study at Weimar cut short by a wrist injury (education recorded as seriously interrupted); one marriage only, to Rudolf Sieber, 17 May 1923, never dissolved - she was widowed at his death 24 June 1976 - long lived apart, hence 'mixed'; one child, Maria, born 13 Dec 1924; Hollywood from April 1930 (Der Blaue Engel premiere and the Paramount move in the same weeks), US citizenship 1939, front-line USO service 1944-45 and the Medal of Freedom; the Las Vegas/concert career from Dec 1953; the Sydney stage fall and surgery Sept 1975; withdrawal to the Avenue Montaigne apartment and roughly a decade bedridden and reclusive from 1979 until her death (renal failure), which drives the 'extended' answers on confinement and on depression/dependency. A21 (speculation) is 'never' and A22 'small' as the least-unsupported readings - neither is well documented; C10 (eyesight), C11 (unearned luck) and C12 (inheritance) carry confidence 2 for the same reason. A36 asks about a period after her death and is answered 'same' as a null. Part D was left unanswered: it is post-reading feedback and cannot be sourced from biography - she never received such a reading.
